stories.headline: Wigan man fined following assault at King’s Lynn nightclub
stories.brief:
A holidaymaker has been ordered to pay compensation and fines after assaulting a security guard in King’s Lynn. Forty-nine-year-old Matthew Crompton, from Wigan, appeared at Lynn Magistrates’ Court on Thursday. He admitted to a charge of assault by beating following an incident at Dr Thirsty’s nightclub on Norfolk Street in the early hours of Sunday, September 6.

The court heard that Crompton, who was visiting the area, punched a member of door staff in the face after being ejected from the venue. His solicitor stated that the punch was intended for a different guard. Crompton must pay £300 in compensation, a £750 fine, a £300 victim surcharge, and £85 in court costs.

stories.headline: Delays expected for revamped leisure centre
stories.brief: Residents in the Fens may face a significant wait before they can use their local leisure centre. Reports indicate that the facility, which is currently undergoing a revamp, could remain closed for up to two years. No further details regarding the specific location or the reasons for the extended timeline have been provided at this stage.

stories.headline: Second man charged following Cambridgeshire burglaries
stories.brief: A second man has been charged in connection with a series of burglaries across Cambridgeshire. The charges follow a recent spate of incidents reported throughout the county. Police have confirmed the development as the investigation into the offences continues.

stories.headline: Lincolnshire regeneration plans approved
stories.brief: A major regeneration project aimed at improving towns across Lincolnshire has been officially approved. The ambitious vision, which focuses on development and local improvements, has now been given the green light. Further details regarding the specific towns involved and the timeline for these works are expected to follow as the project progresses.

stories.headline: Investigation launched following bus incident in Peterborough
stories.brief: A health and safety investigation is underway after a young boy fell from a double-decker bus in Peterborough. Authorities are currently looking into the circumstances surrounding the incident. No further details regarding the condition of the child or the specific location of the event have been released at this time.

stories.headline: New online radio station launches for the Fens
stories.brief: A new independent online radio station, Fenland Angels Radio, has officially launched. Operating 24 hours a day, the station aims to serve Wisbech and the wider Fens, including parts of West Norfolk. Founded by Nathaniel Daw, the service focuses on music, local stories, and community engagement. The team is currently developing its coverage of local events and interviews, and is inviting members of the public to get involved and develop their broadcasting skills. While the station is currently available online, the team is exploring future options for DAB broadcasting. Listeners can access the station through its website.

stories.headline: Man charged following incident at King’s Lynn Railway Station
stories.brief:
A 34-year-old man has been charged with assaulting three police officers following an incident at King’s Lynn Railway Station. Reuben Skinner, of Checker Street in Lynn, faces three counts of assault after officers were called to reports of a man with a head injury on Saturday evening. 

Police have confirmed that no weapons were involved in the incident, dismissing online speculation regarding a stabbing. Mr Skinner was arrested at the station and later taken to the Queen Elizabeth Hospital for treatment. He has been released on bail and is due to appear at Lynn Magistrates’ Court on November 19. Enquiries into how the man sustained his initial injury remain ongoing.

stories.headline: Potential housing for asylum seekers in Fenland
stories.brief: Reports suggest that Fenland could potentially accommodate up to 200 asylum seekers. The information, which originated from the BBC, is currently being discussed regarding the possibility of housing this number of people within the district. No further details have been confirmed at this stage regarding specific locations or timelines for such a proposal. We will continue to monitor the situation for any updates that may affect local residents.

stories.headline: Peterborough United Women climb National League table
stories.brief: Peterborough United Women are enjoying a successful run of form. The team is currently moving up the National League standings, reaching a series of notable milestones during their recent campaign.

stories.headline: Plans revealed for major wind farm project in Shippea Hill
stories.brief: A new wind farm development has been proposed for Shippea Hill. The project is estimated to cost more than £100 million. Further details regarding the scale and timeline of the construction are expected to emerge as the planning process continues. Residents are advised to keep an eye on local planning portals for updates on how this significant infrastructure investment might impact the surrounding area.

stories.headline: Fifteen road closures announced across Cambridgeshire
stories.brief: Motorists travelling across Cambridgeshire are being advised of fifteen separate road closures taking place throughout this week. The disruptions, reported by Peterborough Matters, may affect travel plans for those commuting across the county. Drivers are encouraged to check their routes before setting off to avoid potential delays caused by these works. No specific locations or durations for the closures have been provided at this time, so residents are urged to remain alert for local signage and traffic updates while travelling in the area.

stories.headline: Peterborough Sports extend unbeaten streak to ten matches
stories.brief: Peterborough Sports have reached a ten-game unbeaten run following their latest fixture. Despite the positive result, the club’s manager has expressed frustration regarding the team's performance. The side continues its campaign amidst a busy schedule of midweek non-league football matches across the region.

stories.headline: Cambridgeshire foster carers recognised for long service
stories.brief: More than 50 foster carers from across Cambridgeshire have been formally honoured for their dedication. Collectively, the group has provided 450 years of service to the local community. The recognition highlights the significant contribution these individuals have made to the lives of children in care throughout the region.

stories.headline: Air ambulance called to Long Sutton
stories.brief: An air ambulance has landed in Long Sutton. The incident was reported by the Fenland Citizen. No further details regarding the nature of the emergency or the condition of those involved have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Concerns raised over dust levels at Saxon Pit in Whittlesey
stories.brief: Residents in Whittlesey are raising concerns regarding dust emissions at the Saxon Pit site. Reports indicate that the situation has led to claims involving the use of public funds. Local authorities are currently facing scrutiny over the management of the site and the potential impact of the dust on the surrounding area. Further details regarding the nature of these claims and any planned action remain under discussion. We will continue to monitor the situation as more information becomes available for the community.

stories.headline: Peterborough village may get new milk vending machine
stories.brief: Plans are being considered for the installation of a milk vending machine in a Peterborough village. The proposal, reported by the Peterborough Fenland Edge News, suggests the facility could soon be available to local residents. No specific location or start date for the service has been confirmed at this stage.

stories.headline: A10 Cambridge to Ely upgrade plans removed from project list
stories.brief: Plans to upgrade the A10 between Cambridge and Ely have been removed from the official list of road projects. The decision has been met with disappointment following the announcement. The route remains a key transport link for commuters and residents travelling across the region. No further details regarding the future of the scheme have been provided at this stage.

stories.headline: March business claims lack of belief hinders black entrepreneurs
stories.brief: A company based in March has highlighted the challenges facing black business owners. According to the firm, known as Rayo, a lack of belief is currently holding back entrepreneurs from the black community. The business shared these views regarding the obstacles faced by black-owned enterprises in the region.

stories.headline: Dispute continues over Aldreth bus services
stories.brief: A disagreement regarding bus services in Aldreth remains unresolved. Despite the submission of letters and a petition from the public, the issue has led to a heated exchange involving the Mayor. Reports indicate that the Mayor has publicly challenged the accuracy of claims made by those involved in the dispute. No further details regarding the specific nature of the service changes or the next steps for the campaign have been provided at this time.

stories.headline: Obituary notice for Long Sutton resident Rex Richardson
stories.brief: An obituary has been published for Rex Richardson, a resident of Long Sutton in Lincolnshire. The notice, which appeared in the Spalding Guardian, commemorates the life of Mr. Richardson following his passing in 2020. No further details regarding his life or funeral arrangements have been provided in the public record.

stories.headline: Funds raised for Fenland man in Spanish hospital
stories.brief: A fundraising appeal has reached three thousand pounds to support a Fenland man currently receiving treatment in a Spanish hospital. The individual, described as a deeply loved member of the community, is reported to be fighting for his life. Further details regarding the man's identity or the specific circumstances of his hospitalisation have not been released. The funds were gathered to assist with his ongoing care while he remains abroad.

stories.headline: Mayor suggests Peterborough university road project remains a possibility
stories.brief: The Mayor has indicated that plans for a new road serving the university in Peterborough could still go ahead. While details remain limited, the comments suggest the infrastructure project is still under consideration by local authorities. Further updates on the proposal are expected as discussions continue regarding the development of the university site and its surrounding transport links.

stories.headline: New £110,000 annual fund launched for Cambridgeshire families
stories.brief: A new financial support scheme has been announced for families across Cambridgeshire. Council leader Rayo confirmed that a fund worth £110,000 per year is being established to provide timely assistance to local households. The initiative aims to offer support to those in need throughout the region.

stories.headline: Cambridgeshire man charged following incident near nursery
stories.brief: A man from Cambridgeshire has been named following an accusation of indecent exposure. The individual is alleged to have masturbated in a bush located outside a nursery. The report was published by Peterborough Matters. No further details regarding the identity of the man or the specific location of the nursery have been released at this time.

stories.headline: MasterChef star returns to King’s Lynn for special menu
stories.brief:
MasterChef: The Professionals semi-finalist Polly Norman has returned to her roots in Norfolk for two special evenings at King’s Lynn Golf Club. The 24-year-old from Upwell, who began her career at the club as a teenager, teamed up with head chef Liam Nicol to prepare a four-course menu featuring local game and coastal produce. 

Polly, who now works at Simpson’s in the Strand in London, previously worked as an assistant professional at the golf club before pursuing a culinary career. She says she hopes to eventually return to the county permanently to open her own gastropub on the Norfolk coast.

stories.headline: Deliberate rubbish fire reported in Fenland
stories.brief: Fire crews have attended an incident involving burning rubbish near a road in the Fens. Officials have confirmed that the blaze was started deliberately. No further details regarding the exact location or any potential damage have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Public invited to share views on future of Norfolk hospital services
stories.brief:
The Norfolk and Waveney University Hospitals Group has launched a new campaign titled Case for Change. The initiative aims to plan how hospital care is delivered across the region for future generations. While officials state that no decisions regarding service changes have been made, they are encouraging the public to share their experiences via an independent Healthwatch survey. The survey remains open until Friday, November 6.

In other news, the Queen Elizabeth Hospital recently held its annual Team QEH Awards, presenting 14 prizes to staff members. Additionally, the hospital has begun its seasonal flu vaccination campaign for staff, urging those eligible to get protected ahead of the winter months. Further details on the survey can be found on the group's website.

stories.headline: Peterborough United fans react to Robbie Savage appointment
stories.brief: Supporters of Peterborough United have expressed enthusiasm following the appointment of Robbie Savage as the club's new manager. Fans are welcoming the change in leadership, with many describing the team’s current style of play as a return to the club's reputation for being great entertainers.

stories.headline: East Cambridgeshire District Council leader seeks devolution pilot status
stories.brief: The leader of East Cambridgeshire District Council, Councillor Anna Bailey, has formally requested that the government designate the region as a devolution pilot area. The proposal aims to secure greater local control over decision-making and resources for the district. Councillor Bailey has outlined her reasons for pursuing this status, suggesting that a pilot scheme would benefit the area by allowing for more tailored governance. Further details regarding the potential impact of this move on local services and administration are expected as the request is considered by central government officials.

stories.headline: Long Sutton pensioner remanded in custody
stories.brief: A 74-year-old resident from Long Sutton has been remanded in custody. The decision was made following a court appearance at Lincoln Magistrates’ Court. No further details regarding the case have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Potential plans for two new wind farms in Cambridgeshire
stories.brief: Proposals have emerged for the construction of two large-scale wind farms. The projects are earmarked for locations within Cambridgeshire and along the county border. Further details regarding the specific sites or the timeline for these developments have not yet been released.

stories.headline: Campaign launches to improve child visibility as clocks go back
stories.brief:
A new safety initiative, Be Bright Be Seen, is offering thousands of free reflective keyrings to schools, youth groups, and sports clubs across the region. Sponsored by Ashwood Homes, the campaign aims to help children remain visible to motorists as the nights draw in. With the clocks changing this Sunday, October 25, organisers are encouraging the use of reflective gear and bright clothing for pedestrians and cyclists.

Teachers and youth leaders can apply for an allocation of the keyrings online at the Fenland Citizen website. Applications close this Sunday. The campaign follows recent national data highlighting a rise in road traffic injuries, emphasising the importance of staying visible during the darker winter months.

stories.headline: South Lynn man admits assault following domestic dispute
stories.brief:
A 48-year-old man from South Lynn has pleaded guilty to common assault at Lynn Magistrates’ Court. Cornelius Doddy, of Wisbech Road, admitted to threatening his ex-partner with an ironing board during an argument on July 29. The court heard that the dispute began in a car and continued at their home, where the defendant was reportedly intoxicated. No injuries were sustained during the incident.

In mitigation, the court was told that tensions regarding a potential restaurant venture had contributed to the disagreement. Magistrates have ordered a pre-sentence report, and Mr Doddy has been released on conditional bail. He is due to return to court for sentencing on December 1.

stories.headline: Water supply disruption reported in Littleport
stories.brief:
Residents in Littleport are currently experiencing a loss of water supply following a burst water main. According to reports from the Ely East Cambridgeshire News, the incident has left homes and businesses in the area without water. 

Engineers are working to address the issue, though a timeline for when supplies will be fully restored has not yet been confirmed. Those living in the affected area are advised to check local updates for further information as the situation develops.

stories.headline: Long Sutton travel agents prepare for Santa
stories.brief: Staff at a travel agency in Long Sutton have been busy preparing for the festive season by packing a suitcase for Santa Claus. The local team organised the special display to mark the arrival of Christmas. Residents in the area can view the festive luggage at the branch as part of their seasonal preparations.

stories.headline: Seven-year-old boy dies following incident in Wimblington
stories.brief: A seven-year-old boy has died following reports of a child in the water at Wimblington. Emergency services were called to the scene to respond to the incident. No further details regarding the circumstances have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Rail disruption reported between Peterborough and Doncaster
stories.brief: Passengers travelling by rail this Sunday are being advised of disruption to LNER services. The issues are affecting the line running between Peterborough and Doncaster. Those planning to travel on this route are encouraged to check their journey details before setting off, as the service alterations may impact travel times across the region.

stories.headline: Anglian Water issues update on East Cambridgeshire supply problems
stories.brief:
Residents in East Cambridgeshire are facing ongoing water supply issues today. Anglian Water has released an update regarding the situation, though specific details on the cause or the number of affected properties remain limited. The utility company is currently working to resolve the disruption across the region. 

Customers are advised to check the Anglian Water website for the latest information and updates on when their service is expected to return to normal. We will bring you more on this story as further details become available.

stories.headline: Company denies environmental charges in Long Sutton
stories.brief: A company is contesting environmental charges relating to two sites in Long Sutton. The firm has entered formal denials regarding the allegations brought against them. No further details regarding the nature of the charges or the identity of the business have been released at this stage.

stories.headline: Ten road closures planned across Cambridgeshire this week
stories.brief: Motorists travelling across Cambridgeshire are being advised to plan their journeys carefully over the coming days. A total of ten road closures are scheduled to take place across the county throughout this week. Drivers are encouraged to check local travel updates before setting off to avoid potential delays caused by these works.

stories.headline: West Norfolk schools support mental health campaign
stories.brief:
Pupils and staff across several West Norfolk schools have marked World Mental Health Day by taking part in the ‘Hello Yellow’ campaign. Participants wore bright colours to raise awareness and funds for the charity Young Minds. At West Lynn Primary School, children and staff held a special assembly and completed mental health-related classroom activities. 

Other schools within the West Norfolk Academies Trust also joined the initiative, including Smithdon High School in Hunstanton, St Clement’s High School in Terrington St Clement, and Clenchwarton Primary. The schools shared donation links via their newsletters and websites to support the charity’s work. West Lynn Primary typically raises around £200 for the cause during this annual event.

stories.headline: Two men released following imitation firearm arrest
stories.brief: Lincolnshire Police have released two men without charge following an investigation into an imitation firearm. Officers had previously arrested the pair in connection with the incident. No further action will be taken against them.

stories.headline: Cambridgeshire man in critical condition in Spain
stories.brief: A man from Cambridgeshire is currently in a coma and fighting for his life while in Spain. Reports indicate the individual is receiving medical treatment abroad, though no further details regarding his identity or the circumstances surrounding his condition have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Emergency services respond to river incident in King's Lynn
stories.brief:
Emergency crews were called to the River Great Ouse in King's Lynn on Saturday afternoon following reports of a person in the water. The alarm was raised by the local ferry team at 3:04pm. By the time the Hunstanton Coastguard Rescue Team arrived at South Quay, the individual had been recovered from the river and was receiving medical attention from paramedics. 

The incident involved a multi-agency response, including the East of England Ambulance Service, Norfolk Fire and Rescue Service, and Norfolk Constabulary. Once the person was confirmed safe, all teams were stood down. The Coastguard is reminding the public to dial 999 and ask for the Coastguard if they spot anyone in difficulty along the coast.

stories.headline: Peterborough United draw with Burton Albion
stories.brief: Peterborough United have finished their latest League One fixture with a draw. The match against Burton Albion ended with a final score of two-all.

stories.headline: Cambridgeshire teenager secures bronze medal in Spanish slingshot competition
stories.brief: A teenager from Cambridgeshire has achieved a bronze medal at a slingshot tournament held in Spain. The local competitor reached the podium following two separate shoot-offs during the event. This result marks a historic achievement for the participant in the sport.

stories.headline: Care home staff in Long Sutton and Spalding receive awards
stories.brief: Staff members working at care homes in Long Sutton and Spalding have been formally recognised for their service. According to reports from the Spalding South Holland News, employees at these local facilities have received awards for their ongoing work. No further details regarding the specific nature of the accolades or the individuals involved have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Investigation launched after teenager falls from bus in Wimblington
stories.brief: An investigation is underway following an incident in Wimblington where a 14-year-old boy fell from a bus window. Authorities are currently looking into the circumstances surrounding the event. No further details regarding the boy's condition or the specific cause of the fall have been released at this time.

stories.headline: North Lynn man charged following bus station incident
stories.brief:
A 20-year-old man has been charged following an incident at King’s Lynn bus station on Monday evening. Daniel Neves, of Walpole Road, faces two counts of assaulting emergency workers and two charges of criminal damage relating to a police officer’s watch and body-worn camera. 

The charges follow an encounter where officers attempted to seize an illegal e-scooter. West Norfolk Police have thanked members of the public for their assistance during the arrest. Mr Neves has been bailed and is due to appear at Lynn Magistrates’ Court on November 12. Police say they are increasing foot patrols at the bus station to address reports of anti-social behaviour as the evenings grow darker.

stories.headline: Deliberate fire at derelict building
stories.brief: Police are investigating a fire at a derelict building, which is believed to have been started deliberately. The incident was reported by the March Chatteris Whittlesey News. No further details regarding the location or the extent of the damage have been released at this time. Authorities are continuing their inquiries into the circumstances surrounding the blaze.

stories.headline: Nominations open for 2027 King’s Lynn and West Norfolk Mayor’s Business Awards
stories.brief:
Nominations are now being accepted for the 2027 King’s Lynn and West Norfolk Mayor’s Business Awards. Organised by the Lynn News and Your Local Paper, the event features 12 categories, including the Business Leader of the Year, which is sponsored by British Sugar. This specific category is open to third-party nominations only.

The awards ceremony will be held at the Alive Corn Exchange in Lynn on Friday, March 5. Businesses may enter up to two categories, with the deadline for submissions set for 5pm on Friday, November 27. Judges will also select an overall Mayor’s Business of the Year from the category winners, to be announced during the event.

stories.headline: Cambridgeshire restaurants secure four national awards
stories.brief: Restaurants across Cambridgeshire have been recognised at the 2026 national Asian food awards. Local establishments collectively secured four titles during the ceremony. The success was reported by the Ely East Cambridgeshire News.

stories.headline: Anti-racist demonstration held in Cambridge
stories.brief: An anti-racist unity demonstration is taking place in Cambridge today. The event, reported by Cambsnews, has brought people together in the city for the protest. No further details regarding the scale or specific location of the gathering have been provided at this time.

stories.headline: West Norfolk Council deputy leader calls for new approach to town centre revival
stories.brief:
West Norfolk Council’s deputy leader, Simon Ring, says the future of King’s Lynn must move beyond retail to succeed. Welcoming a new £210 million government high street regeneration package, Councillor Ring stated that the town needs to adapt to modern habits by creating a mixed-use centre where people live, work, and spend their leisure time. 

The council is already working to bring long-term vacant buildings, such as the former Post Office and Debenhams, back into use. Meanwhile, North West Norfolk MP James Wild is supporting a campaign to cut business costs and tackle crime, highlighting concerns from local firms regarding business rates and energy bills. The council is currently awaiting details on how much funding may be allocated to the area.

stories.headline: Celebrating King’s Lynn’s historic figures
stories.brief:
King’s Lynn is home to three statues honouring figures who shaped both the town and the wider world. The collection includes a bronze tribute to King John on New Conduit Street, unveiled in 2016 to mark the monarch’s 1204 charter which granted the town its independence. 

The town also features a statue of explorer Captain George Vancouver on Purfleet Quay, commemorating his extensive mapping of the Northwest Pacific coastline. Finally, a statue at Guanock Place celebrates Frederick Savage, a renowned engineer and former mayor who became famous for his pioneering work on steam-powered fairground rides. These landmarks serve as a permanent reminder of the town’s rich history and the significant contributions of these three men.

stories.headline: Peterborough murder trial underway
stories.brief: A murder trial is currently taking place in Peterborough. During proceedings at court, it was alleged that the defendant smiled following a stabbing incident. The case continues as the legal process moves forward.

stories.headline: A10 Cambridge to Ely upgrade project cancelled
stories.brief: Plans to upgrade the A10 between Cambridge and Ely have been removed from the official development list. The decision has been met with disappointment, as the route will no longer receive the previously proposed improvements. No further details regarding the cancellation have been provided at this stage.

stories.headline: Urgent improvements required at local school
stories.brief: A new report has highlighted that a school in the region is in need of urgent improvement. The findings, published by LincsOnline, describe the assessment of the educational facility as damning. No further details regarding the specific identity of the school or the nature of the concerns have been released at this time.

stories.headline: King’s Lynn man to face trial over Wisbech exposure charges
stories.brief:
A 54-year-old man from King’s Lynn is set to stand trial following allegations of indecent exposure in Wisbech. Simon Wells, of Oak Avenue, appeared at Lynn Magistrates’ Court on Thursday. He faces charges relating to multiple incidents between June 1 and September 1 of this year, where he is accused of intentionally exposing himself to cause alarm or distress.

Mr. Wells entered a not guilty plea and has been released on conditional bail, which prohibits him from contacting the victim. The case has been adjourned, and he is due to return to the same court on January 14 for trial.

stories.headline: King’s Lynn Waterstones names Book of the Week
stories.brief:
Waterstones in King’s Lynn has selected ‘Craftland: A Journey Through Britain's Living Past’ by James Fox as its current Book of the Week. The publication explores the work of remaining master craftspeople across the country, ranging from wheelwrights to silversmiths. The author examines how traditional trades and vanishing skills have helped shape British national identity and regional culture over hundreds of years. 

The store on Norfolk Street has also released its latest top ten list, which includes titles by authors such as Elly Griffiths, Anthony Horowitz, and Sarah Vaughan. Readers can find more information on these selections by visiting the King’s Lynn branch.

stories.headline: Improvements planned for Spalding site
stories.brief: A derelict site in Spalding is set for a transformation. According to reports from the Spalding South Holland News, the area is undergoing a bright new look. The project aims to improve the appearance of the location, which had previously fallen into a run-down state. No further details regarding the specific nature of the work or a completion date have been provided at this time.

stories.headline: Public demonstration planned for Queen Elizabeth Hospital services
stories.brief:
A public demonstration is taking place this Saturday at the Tuesday Market Place in King’s Lynn. Organisers are inviting residents to join a "human queue" between 11.30am and 12pm to show support for the Queen Elizabeth Hospital. Councillors Rob Colwell and Jo Rust are encouraging people to attend to highlight the importance of the hospital’s A&E, critical care, and maternity units. 

The event follows concerns that these services could be at risk. However, some local officials have expressed reassurance after meeting with Healthwatch Norfolk, noting that no final decisions have been made. Attendees are encouraged to bring signs showing their travel time to the hospital to demonstrate the impact of potential service changes on the local community.

stories.headline: New Amazon distribution centre opens
stories.brief: A new Amazon distribution centre has officially opened. The facility represents an investment of £107 million.

stories.headline: Funding cancelled for major Cambridgeshire A-road improvements
stories.brief: Plans to upgrade a major A-road in Cambridgeshire have been cancelled. According to reports from the Ely East Cambridgeshire News, funding previously allocated for improvements to the route has been scrapped. No further details regarding the specific road affected or the reasons behind the decision have been provided at this time.

stories.headline: Travellers arrive at site near busy Lincolnshire road
stories.brief: A group of travellers has established an encampment close to a busy road in Lincolnshire. Reports indicate the group has pitched up in the area, though specific details regarding the exact location or the number of people involved have not been confirmed. Motorists travelling through the region are advised to remain aware of the situation. Further updates will be provided as more information becomes available.

stories.headline: Police investigation following break-in at services
stories.brief: Police have made an arrest following a break-in at a services location. Officers are currently investigating the incident. No further details regarding the location or the identity of the individual arrested have been released at this time.

stories.headline: King’s Lynn care provider placed in special measures
stories.brief:
A King’s Lynn-based home care service, Dedicated Care East Anglia, has been downgraded to "inadequate" by the Care Quality Commission. The watchdog found the provider breached five legal regulations, including those regarding safeguarding and safe care. Inspectors raised concerns over staff using faulty equipment and failing to follow care plans. One report noted a staff member left a distressed client to smoke outside.

The service, based at Tansley Business Park, is now in special measures and will be closely monitored. While the firm expressed disappointment and is challenging some findings, it has appointed external experts to review its processes. The CQC noted that some families reported feeling their relatives were treated with dignity and respect.

stories.headline: Second class stamp prices fixed until 2028
stories.brief: Royal Mail has confirmed that the price of a second class stamp will remain unchanged for the next few years. The cost is set to stay at its current rate until March 2028. This update provides long-term clarity for households and businesses across the Fens who rely on postal services for their daily correspondence.

stories.headline: Magician tours King’s Lynn running clubs for YouTube project
stories.brief:
A local magician is visiting every running club in and around King’s Lynn to document his experiences for his YouTube channel, Josh Maddocks Runs. Josh Maddocks, who previously raised funds for Macmillan, says he launched the project to see if local groups were as intimidating as they might appear to outsiders. Having already visited eight clubs, including the Custom House Social Run and Ryston Runners, he reports that all groups have been welcoming to runners of all abilities. 

Mr Maddocks, who is training for the London Marathon alongside his wife Emily, hopes his videos will encourage others to join local groups, noting that there is a suitable club for everyone regardless of fitness levels.

stories.headline: Potential job losses at McCain Foods in Whittlesey
stories.brief: McCain Foods has announced plans to change its manufacturing operations at its site in Whittlesey. The company has indicated that these proposed adjustments could put a number of local jobs at risk. No further details regarding the scale of the potential redundancies or the specific nature of the operational changes have been confirmed at this stage.

stories.headline: A10 Cambridge to Ely upgrade plans removed from project list
stories.brief: Plans to upgrade the A10 between Cambridge and Ely have been cancelled. The project has been officially removed from the list of planned road improvements. The decision has been met with disappointment, as the route remains a key transport link for those travelling across the Fens. No further details regarding the cancellation have been provided at this time.

stories.headline: Police investigate armed robbery at Long Sutton newsagent
stories.brief: Lincolnshire Police are investigating an armed robbery at a newsagent in Long Sutton. A person armed with a knife entered the shop and stole a quantity of cash and cigarettes. Officers are currently looking into the incident. Anyone with information regarding the robbery is encouraged to contact the authorities.

stories.headline: Former Wisbech Town FC president returns to watch match
stories.brief:
A resident of Orchard House Care Home in Wisbech has enjoyed a special return to his former football club. John Petch, who served as president of Wisbech Town Football Club for 16 years, expressed a wish to see his hometown team play once again. Staff from the care home arranged for Mr Petch and his wife, Sheila, to attend Saturday’s match, which included lunch at Bygones. 

Mr Petch, who stepped down from his role in 2020 after nearly 60 years of service, was greeted by many familiar faces, including club chairman Paul Brenchley. He described the experience as a fantastic day, made even better by a victory for the home side.

stories.headline: New NHS guidance changes ward access for Norfolk hospitals
stories.brief:
Norfolk hospitals, including the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn, are updating their policies following new guidance from NHS England. The rules require that single-sex hospital services, such as wards, toilets, and bathrooms, be provided based on a patient's biological sex rather than gender identity. 

The Norfolk and Waveney University Hospitals Group says it is reviewing the implications of the guidance to ensure compliance. The new policy, which also applies to mental health facilities and GP surgeries, includes exceptions for areas like A&E and critical care. Where biological sex placement is not clinically appropriate, hospitals are instructed to provide alternatives, such as single rooms. Trusts have been asked to implement these changes at pace.

stories.headline: Long Sutton pedestrian crossing to be refurbished
stories.brief: Lincolnshire County Council has announced plans to refurbish the pedestrian crossing on High Street in Long Sutton. The local authority confirmed the upcoming works as part of its ongoing maintenance programme for the area. Residents and motorists travelling through the town centre are advised to prepare for potential changes to the road layout while the improvements are carried out. Further details regarding the specific start date and any traffic management measures will be provided by the council in due course.

stories.headline: Campaigners oppose school leisure centre closure
stories.brief: Local campaigners are challenging a decision to close a school leisure centre. The move has been described as a difficult start to the new year for those who use the facility. The Spalding South Holland News reports that the school’s decision to shut the site has prompted a fight from those opposed to the closure. No further details regarding the timeline for the shutdown or the specific school involved have been confirmed at this stage.

stories.headline: Concerns raised over potential Queen Elizabeth Hospital service changes
stories.brief:
Independent borough councillor Jo Rust has raised concerns regarding a strategic review of Norfolk’s three hospitals. A leaked report suggests potential plans to centralise Accident and Emergency services in Norwich and downgrade facilities at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn. 

Senior doctors have warned that such changes could lead to a workforce crisis and increased distress for patients. The hospital’s chief executive, Lesley Dwyer, has cited changing healthcare needs and birth rates as reasons for reviewing maternity, ICU, and A&E services. A protest is planned for this Saturday at 11.30am at the Tuesday Market Place in King’s Lynn. Residents are being encouraged to share their views by emailing Healthwatch Norfolk.

stories.headline: New indoor cycling studio to open in Cambridgeshire
stories.brief: A new indoor cycling studio is set to open in a Cambridgeshire town. The facility is being described as the first of its kind in the area. Further details regarding the exact location and opening date have not yet been released.

stories.headline: Looking back at local news from the archives
stories.brief:
We are looking back at local stories from the archives this week. In 1994, staff from the Methwold firm Howard Long International raised £2,600 for the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn. The money, collected through a sponsored three-legged pub crawl, was used to furnish a quiet room near the accident and emergency department.

Meanwhile, in 2001, protestors gathered outside RAF Feltwell for a peaceful vigil. Around 20 people took part in the demonstration, which was part of a global movement opposing the militarisation of space and the American National Missile Defence plans. The event also served as a response to the conflict in Afghanistan.

stories.headline: Schools close in Cambridgeshire town due to water supply issues
stories.brief: Several schools in a Cambridgeshire town have been forced to close today. The closures follow reports of a loss of water supply in the area. Parents and guardians are advised to check with their individual schools for further updates regarding reopening times and arrangements for pupils.

stories.headline: Cambridgeshire County Council cuts funding for handyperson service
stories.brief: Cambridgeshire County Council has decided to withdraw funding for the local handyperson service. The move follows a decision by the local authority that will impact the provision of support previously managed by Age UK. Residents who rely on this service for assistance with minor home repairs and adaptations may be affected by the change. Further details regarding the timeline for the withdrawal and any alternative support options have not yet been provided by the council.

stories.headline: Police investigation continues into Wisbech murder
stories.brief:
Police inquiries are ongoing following the death of 37-year-old Atis Bleive in Wisbech. Officers were called to a property on Osborne Road at approximately 4pm on January 19, where Mr Bleive was pronounced dead at the scene. A post-mortem examination confirmed he died from a stab wound to the abdomen.

Two local people were arrested on suspicion of murder. A 41-year-old man was released under investigation, while a 45-year-old woman remains on bail until December 29. Detectives have confirmed that the investigation into the circumstances surrounding the death is continuing.

stories.headline: Man sentenced for murder in Cambridgeshire
stories.brief: A man has been sentenced for murder following an investigation by Cambridgeshire Constabulary. The force described the incident as a cold-blooded killing. No further details regarding the identity of the individual or the location of the sentencing have been released at this time.

stories.headline: West Norfolk Council declines to detail swimming pool planning costs
stories.brief:
West Norfolk Council has declined a request to provide a breakdown of the £845,609 spent on planning a new swimming pool at Lynnsport. The local authority stated that the information is commercially sensitive and that releasing details could prejudice future contract negotiations. 

The proposed £23 million facility is intended to replace the existing St James Swimming Pool. Council leader Alistair Beales defended the expenditure, noting that planning in a flood zone involves uncertain ground conditions. While the council approved the planning budget last month, officials emphasised that the project remains in the development phase. Previous attempts to relocate the pool to Lynnsport were abandoned after feasibility studies suggested costs could exceed £45 million.

stories.headline: Man charged following Cambridgeshire burglaries
stories.brief: Police have named a man who has been charged in connection with a series of burglaries across Cambridgeshire. The charges follow a recent spate of incidents reported throughout the county. Authorities confirmed the identity of the individual as part of their ongoing response to the offences. Further details regarding the case are expected to emerge as legal proceedings continue.

stories.headline: Lincolnshire village identified as one of the country's most deprived areas
stories.brief: A village in Lincolnshire has been highlighted as one of the most deprived locations in the UK. According to a report from the Spalding South Holland News, the area is being described as a "forgotten" community. The findings place the village among the most disadvantaged regions across the country. No further details regarding the specific location or the criteria used for the assessment have been provided at this time.

stories.headline: Police arrest suspect following March service station break-in
stories.brief: Police have made an arrest following a break-in at a service station in March. Officers are currently investigating the circumstances surrounding the incident. No further details regarding the identity of the individual arrested or the extent of the damage have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Police appeal following serious collision in Sawtry
stories.brief:
Police are appealing for witnesses after a serious collision between a lorry and a motorbike in Sawtry yesterday. The incident occurred at approximately 12:50pm on the B1043 Old North Road, involving a red Volvo HGV and a black Kawasaki motorbike. The motorcyclist, a 23-year-old man from Yaxley, was taken to Addenbrooke’s Hospital with life-threatening injuries. 

The lorry driver, a 76-year-old man from Wisbech, was arrested on suspicion of causing serious injury by careless driving and has been released on bail until January 4. Officers are urging anyone with information or dashcam footage to contact the police via their website or by calling 101, quoting reference 35/77423/26.

stories.headline: Future of West Lynn’s Freebridge Farm site remains uncertain
stories.brief:
The Freebridge Farm restaurant in West Lynn could potentially reopen following a national deal involving its parent company, Whitbread PLC. The site on Clenchwarton Road closed last month as part of a wider move to reduce the number of Brewers Fayre and Beefeater locations across the UK. 

Two hospitality firms, Common Table Group and Queensway Inns, have now acquired over 100 branches between them. While it is not yet confirmed if the West Lynn site is included in this purchase, the new owners plan to begin reopening locations as early as next month. The move is expected to create 1,400 jobs across the country.

stories.headline: Cambridgeshire man charged following incident outside nursery
stories.brief: A man from Cambridgeshire has been named following an accusation of indecent exposure. The individual is alleged to have masturbated in a bush located outside a nursery. Legal proceedings are now underway regarding the incident.

stories.headline: West Norfolk students tackle hospital tech challenges
stories.brief:
Students from five schools across West Norfolk are taking part in the Future Talent Tech Programme. The initiative, delivered by Tech Educators and funded by the local council, tasks young people with solving real-world problems faced by the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn.

Participants are attending workshops to develop skills in coding, AI, and project management. These sessions will continue throughout the autumn, helping students refine their ideas ahead of a final hackathon. The event is scheduled to take place on November 4 and 5 at the Alive Corn Exchange, where teams will pitch their practical solutions to a panel of industry experts.

stories.headline: Police investigate assault on boys in Peterborough
stories.brief: Cambridgeshire Police are investigating an assault involving two boys in Peterborough. Reports indicate that the victims were attacked by men who held keys between their fingers during the incident. Authorities are currently looking into the circumstances surrounding the event. Anyone with information regarding the assault is encouraged to contact the police to assist with their ongoing enquiries.

stories.headline: Plans revealed for major wind farm project in Shippea Hill
stories.brief: A new wind farm development has been proposed for Shippea Hill. The project is estimated to cost more than £100 million. Further details regarding the scale and timeline of the construction are expected to emerge as the planning process continues. Residents are advised to monitor local planning portals for updates on how this significant infrastructure investment might impact the surrounding area.

stories.headline: Olive production begins at Long Sutton farm
stories.brief: A farm in Long Sutton is now producing olives. The Lincolnshire business has successfully adapted to changing climate conditions to cultivate the crop.

stories.headline: Police make arrest following break-in at services
stories.brief: Police have confirmed an arrest has been made following a break-in at a services location. Officers are currently investigating the incident. No further details regarding the location or the identity of the individual arrested have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Wisbech students target top universities
stories.brief:
Sixth form students at Thomas Clarkson Academy in Wisbech are beginning their university applications, with many aiming for highly competitive courses. Current applicants are seeking places to study medicine, veterinary science, law at the University of Cambridge, and computer science at the University of Oxford. The academy reports a record number of applications for 2026, highlighting a growing trend of ambition among students.

To support prospective students, the academy is hosting a Sixth Form Open Evening on Thursday, November 12, starting at 6pm. Families are invited to meet staff, explore available courses, and learn more about the university preparation and enrichment opportunities offered at the school.

stories.headline: Witnesses sought following hit-and-run in King’s Lynn
stories.brief:
Norfolk Police are appealing for information after a hit-and-run incident in King’s Lynn on Sunday evening. At approximately 10:50pm, a dark-coloured 4x4 collided with a parked silver Suzuki Swift on Southgate Street, causing significant damage to the vehicle. Doorbell footage captured the collision, and officers are now working to identify the driver involved.

Anyone who witnessed the incident or possesses relevant dashcam footage is urged to contact Norfolk Police. You can assist the investigation by calling 01603 276220 or emailing RoadCollisionsSupportTeam@Suffolk.police.uk, quoting reference URN 1825752. Alternatively, information can be provided anonymously to Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111.

stories.headline: Long Sutton pair sentenced for Christmas Day assault
stories.brief: A father and son from Long Sutton have avoided prison sentences following an assault that took place on Christmas Day. The pair appeared in court regarding the incident, where it was confirmed they will not be serving time behind bars. No further details regarding the circumstances of the assault or the specific sentences handed down have been released at this time.

stories.headline: Former Peterborough councillors receive public service honour
stories.brief: A group of former Peterborough councillors have been awarded a prestigious honour. The recognition has been granted to acknowledge their long-standing commitment to public service.

stories.headline: Concerns raised over potential water shortages in the region
stories.brief: Residents across the Fens are being warned of a potentially serious water shortage. Reports from the Ely East Cambridgeshire News indicate that supply concerns must be taken seriously to avoid significant issues. No further details regarding specific locations or timeframes have been provided at this stage, but officials are highlighting the importance of addressing these supply worries now. Listeners are advised to stay tuned for any further updates regarding local water infrastructure as more information becomes available.
